(2019) JGR Planets 124:1296-1314 DOI:10.1029/2018JE005876 (journal full text and Supporting Information S1 checked 19/11/2026): section 2.4 p.1302: internal friction angle of lunar pyroclastic deposits (LPD) = 31 deg (mare 28, highland 30), from the angle of repose at the toe of shallow granular flows on two LROC NAC DEMs (Table S4: 'LPD #1' and 'LPD #2', deposits not named; the Aristarchus NAC DEM was used only for the WAC DEM error check). Same terrain elsewhere, not measured at this site; angle of repose = loose material, so a low-side estimate compared with the in-place Moon-wide set (35 deg, Lunar Sourcebook Table 9.14). Aristarchus is the largest of the 8 LPDs studied (Table S1: 49013 km2, 14 boulder tracks); LPD bearing capacity is equal to or higher than mare and highland at 0.19-5 m depth (p.1305, Table S6). Pyroclastic soil density used by the authors: 1.63 g/cm3 (< 30 cm) and 1.85 g/cm3 (> 30 cm) (Table S3, Apollo 15 sample 15010 and Apollo 17 sample 76001). Range 30-50 deg = Moon-wide range (Lunar Sourcebook Table 9.11; NASA SP-330 p.8-1), since Bickel gives no range. Cohesion, kc, kphi, n: Moon-wide set (Bickel assumes c = 1 kPa, not measured).
